basis: Brachial plexus injury causes arm and hand paralysis; weakness reflects nerve injury rather than primary muscle disease.
Inherited keratinization disorder with skin plaques and erythema in 8/8 patients; no established extracutaneous damage.
Inherited neurologic syndrome with intention tremor, ataxia and lipofuscin storage; premature hair graying alone does not establish damaging skin involvement.
Hepatocerebral mitochondrial depletion with neuropathy; pigmentary retinopathy in 2/2 reported patients. Tubulopathy and hearing loss each 1/1, omitted under cap; samples small.
Defining speech delay and strabismus; intellectual disability in 30-79%. Earlobe creases and facial morphology do not establish additional functional organ damage.
Defective beta-globin synthesis causes anemia. Umbrella includes mild forms; skeletal damage and iron-related organ injury chiefly concern severe or transfused disease.
Lysosomal storage with defining liver and splenic infiltration; pulmonary storage/interstitial disease affects most. Neurologic degeneration varies by subtype and is omitted under cap.
Mitochondrial complex I disease spectrum; cardiac, neurologic, ocular and skin abnormalities vary by subtype, with insufficient evidence of their frequency across the umbrella.
Inherited retinal degeneration arising in Bruch's membrane; vascular and neurologic ancestry does not establish separate organ involvement.
Fibroepithelial tumor arising in breast or rarely prostate, both outside the axes. Distant metastases are not common across the benign-to-malignant umbrella.
Glucose transport disorder defined by paroxysmal dyskinesia and progressive spastic paraplegia. Episodic diplopia does not establish direct eye damage.
Cerebral small-vessel arteriopathy with defining subcortical infarction and leukoencephalopathy; bladder symptoms reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Hypertrophic narrowing of the gastric pylorus causes obstruction. Vomiting-related alkalosis does not establish a separate directly damaged organ.
Tumor originates in endocrine pancreatic beta cells. Neuroglycopenic episodes do not establish persistent brain damage; associated MEN1 tumors are separate diseases.
Defining subcutaneous lipomatous overgrowth and partial lipodystrophy. Peripheral neuropathy is variable, without an established frequency meeting the threshold.
FOXE3-related lens cataract, sometimes accompanied by corneal opacity; established manifestations remain ocular.
Inflammatory, typically immune-mediated spinal cord injury; associated motor, sensory and bladder dysfunction arise from the cord lesion.
Localized suppurative infection of urethral glands; urethra belongs to the renal axis.
Splenic tissue necrosis from compromised arterial or venous circulation; both the spleen and its vascular supply define the disease.
Metabolic bone disease with defining skeletal destruction and hearing loss; optic atrophy 30-79%. Dental morphology lacks demonstrated dysfunction; vascular findings omitted under cap.
Defining periosteal bone thickening and pachydermia; skin thickening in 2/2. Diarrhea in 1/2 alone does not establish direct intestinal damage.
Hereditary degenerative white-matter disease with axonal spheroids; no established common extracerebral damage across the subtypes.
Congenital absence of gluteal skeletal muscles; no additional organ involvement established.
Defining thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection. Dural ectasia in 3/4 does not establish neural damage; palate and skeletal morphology alone do not establish functional injury.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with developmental and speech delay in 19/19 and intellectual disability in 10/10. Hypotonia is neurologic; ear shape does not establish ear dysfunction.
